question: to the Commission Saskia Bricmont (Verts/ALE) Subject:

In 2019, the Commission initiated dispute settlement proceedings against South Korea, alleging that it had failed to fulfil its obligations concerning International Labour Organization (ILO) conventions under the bilateral free trade agreement (FTA). The dispute focused on the provision requiring the parties to ‘make continuous and sustained efforts towards the ratification’ of the fundamental ILO conventions. In its report of 20 January 20211, the Panel of Experts issued several recommendations. It stressed that this obligation was not enforceable ‘in the absence of explicit targets or at least any informal understanding on expected milestones towards ratification’ (paragraphs 276 and 278). Since then, the European Parliament2 and the Council3 have recommended adopting ‘detailed, time-bound implementation roadmaps’ as a useful tool to achieve the desired results. Nevertheless, subsequent FTAs have retained the same contentious wording in their TSD chapters. 1.
Why has the Commission not incorporated the Panel of Experts’ findings into subsequent FTAs?
Why has it not used the TSD Committee to agree on implementation roadmaps with partner countries? (If it has, what was the outcome?).
